B1:
Touched fires once per touching body part (feet, legs, torso...) and several times in the same frame/physics step before Destroy takes effect, so several handlers run for the same pickup (3-5 parts x 10). Destroy doesn't stop already-queued events. Fix with a debounce flag set before granting (and server-side script):
```lua
local part = script.Parent
local taken = false
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
  if taken then return end
  local plr = game.Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
  if not plr then return end
  local ls = plr:FindFirstChild("leaderstats"); if not ls then return end
  taken = true
  ls.Coins.Value += 10
  part:Destroy()
end)
```
For respawning pickups use a per-player cooldown table instead of Destroy.
B2: With StreamingEnabled the client only has instances near the player; distant parts of the Hotel model (the Door) are not streamed in yet (or were streamed out, parented to nil), so dot-indexing errors. Fixes: (1) Use WaitForChild with care / handle streaming: `local door = workspace.Map.Buildings:WaitForChild("Hotel"):WaitForChild("Door", 10)` and nil-check, or better listen with CollectionService tag 'Door' (GetTagged + GetInstanceAddedSignal/RemovedSignal) so doors are wired as they stream in and cleaned up when out. (2) Make the model stream as a unit/always present: Hotel.ModelStreamingMode = Atomic (whole model arrives together) or Persistent for essentials (always sent), or do Touched detection on the server instead of the client.
B3: Bugs: (1) Always returns PurchaseGranted even when pcall failed -> charged, nothing saved, Roblox never retries. (2) No idempotency: no PurchaseId record, so a retried/re-delivered receipt grants again (double coins). (3) GetAsync+SetAsync race (non-atomic); should be UpdateAsync. (4) plr may be nil (player left) -> error indexing plr.UserId; should return NotProcessedYet. (5) No product check (any ProductId gives 100). (6) Separate store from the player's session data can conflict with the profile's own saves. Correct: look up player; if missing return NotProcessedYet; check info.ProductId; in one UpdateAsync on the player's profile, if PurchaseId already in processed list do nothing, else add coins + record PurchaseId; only if that succeeds return PurchaseGranted, otherwise NotProcessedYet. Only one script sets ProcessReceipt.
B4: Remote arguments are serialized: metatables are stripped (and functions can't be sent), so the client gets a plain table {Name, Ammo} without Weapon methods -> w:Fire is nil. Instances are sent as references; an instance in ServerStorage doesn't exist on the client (not replicated), so it arrives as nil. Fix: send plain data (e.g. {Name='Rifle', Ammo=30}) and reconstruct on the client with a shared ModuleScript class in ReplicatedStorage: `local w = setmetatable(data, Weapon)` (or Weapon.new(data)). For the part, put it in ReplicatedStorage/workspace (replicated) or send an identifier and clone a client-side copy; or clone it into a replicated location before firing.
B5:
workspace:Raycast's direction is not unit: its magnitude is the ray length. Using .Unit makes the ray only 1 stud long, so it almost never reaches the target. Fix: scale the direction to the desired range and exclude the shooter:
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {shooterCharacter}
local dir = (target - origin).Unit * 300 -- max range
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if r then print(r.Instance, r.Position) end
```
B6: When the last player leaves, the server begins shutting down; PlayerRemoving's yielding SetAsync may not finish before the process closes (and shutdowns/updates can close servers with players in them), so the save is cut off. Fix: game:BindToClose(function() ... end) that saves all remaining players' data in parallel (task.spawn each, wait until all done) within the ~30 s shutdown window (aim ~25 s), and also waits for in-flight PlayerRemoving saves; make saves per-player serialized/idempotent so both paths don't collide, use UpdateAsync with retries, autosave periodically, and skip waiting in Studio (RunService:IsStudio()).

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local UseAbility = game.ReplicatedStorage.UseAbility
local COOLDOWN = 2
local lastUse = {} :: {[Player]: number}

UseAbility.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, abilityId)
  if typeof(abilityId) ~= "string" then return end
  local now = os.clock()
  local last = lastUse[player]
  if last and now - last < COOLDOWN then return end -- silently ignore spam
  lastUse[player] = now
  local char = player.Character
  local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  performAbility(player, abilityId)
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
  lastUse[player] = nil -- no leak
end)
```
Cooldown timestamp set before any yields; the server is authoritative.
B8:
```lua
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local store = game:GetService("DataStoreService"):GetDataStore("PlayerData")
local PRODUCTS = { [123456] = function(d) d.Gems = (d.Gems or 0) + 100 end } -- Gems100

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  local grant = PRODUCTS[info.ProductId]
  if not grant then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end -- retried on next join
  local ok, err = pcall(function()
    store:UpdateAsync("player_" .. info.PlayerId, function(data, keyInfo)
      data = data or {}
      data.Receipts = data.Receipts or {}
      if data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return data end -- already granted
      grant(data)
      data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = os.time() -- prune old ones
      return data, keyInfo and keyInfo:GetUserIds(), keyInfo and keyInfo:GetMetadata()
    end)
  end)
  if not ok then warn(err) return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  -- update in-memory session/UI from saved data here
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
```
Single ProcessReceipt in the game; with session-locked profiles, apply via the locked profile and save before returning Granted.

```lua
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.4, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local OPEN = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5, 0)
local CLOSED = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1.5, 0)
menu.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
local current

local function open()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  menu.Position = CLOSED
  menu.Visible = true
  current = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = OPEN})
  current:Play()
end

local function close()
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  local t = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = CLOSED})
  current = t
  t.Completed:Connect(function(state)
    if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and current == t then
      menu.Visible = false
    end
  end)
  t:Play()
end
```

```lua
local MAX_RANGE, DAMAGE = 200, 20
local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
  if typeof(targetPos) ~= "Vector3" or targetPos ~= targetPos then return end
  local char = player.Character
  local head = char and char:FindFirstChild("Head")
  local myHum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not head or not myHum or myHum.Health <= 0 then return end
  local origin = head.Position
  local offset = targetPos - origin
  if offset.Magnitude < 1e-3 then return end
  local params = RaycastParams.new()
  params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {char}
  local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, offset.Unit * MAX_RANGE, params)
  if not result then return end
  local model = result.Instance:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
  local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if hum and hum.Health > 0 then hum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE) end
end
```

```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local TAG = "KillBrick"
local conns = {} :: {[BasePart]: RBXScriptConnection}

local function onAdded(part)
  if not part:IsA("BasePart") or conns[part] then return end
  conns[part] = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local hum = hit.Parent and hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if hum and hum.Health > 0 then hum.Health = 0 end
  end)
end

local function onRemoved(part)
  local c = conns[part]
  if c then c:Disconnect(); conns[part] = nil end
end

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TAG):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TAG):Connect(onRemoved)
for _, p in CollectionService:GetTagged(TAG) do onAdded(p) end
```
RemovedSignal also fires when the part is destroyed, so the table never leaks.

```lua
local TeleportService = game:GetService("TeleportService")
local MAX_ATTEMPTS, DELAY = 4, 2

local function safeTeleport(placeId, players, teleportData)
  local options = Instance.new("TeleportOptions")
  if teleportData then options:SetTeleportData(teleportData) end
  for attempt = 1, MAX_ATTEMPTS do
    local ok, result = pcall(TeleportService.TeleportAsync, TeleportService, placeId, players, options)

  retries[player] = (retries[player] or 0) + 1

  safeTeleport(placeId, {player}, options and options:GetTeleportData())
end)
game.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) retries[p] = nil end)
```

Save player data before teleporting; teleport data is not trusted.
B13: (a) Client -> server: a RemoteEvent (e.g. BuyItem) or RemoteFunction (InvokeServer, if the client wants a success/fail reply) carrying only the item id. The server holds the authoritative coin balance (session data/leaderstats on the server), looks up the price itself, validates type, existence, affordability, rate limit, deducts and grants. (b) Server -> client: a RemoteEvent FireClient (e.g. CoinsChanged) or simply replicated state (leaderstats IntValue / attribute the UI listens to via Changed). Don't use RemoteFunction:InvokeClient: the server yields waiting on the client, which can hang forever (client never returns), error if it disconnects, or return spoofed data, stalling the purchase thread; UI updates are fire-and-forget so an event/replicated value is correct.
B14: Teleport data (TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData) passes through the client: the client can read and modify it, so the destination's GetJoinData().TeleportData is only partially trusted (SourcePlaceId genuine, content client-transmitted) and LocalPlayer:GetTeleportData is untrusted. Never put coins or loadout there as authority. DataStore (session-locked profile): authoritative, persistent; save + release the lock before TeleportAsync, destination loads with UpdateAsync. MemoryStore: fast, short-lived server-written handoff (e.g. a match ticket or chosen loadout keyed by userId, with expiry), trusted because only servers write it. Choice: coins in the DataStore profile (saved before teleport); loadout either in the profile or a MemoryStore entry/ticket; teleport data only for non-sensitive hints (e.g. match id, which the destination validates).
B15: Per-instance Scripts: 610 script copies, each with its own connections/threads; duplicate code that drifts when edited, hard to update, more memory and startup cost, can't easily handle instances created at runtime, and with StreamingEnabled client copies break. Tag-driven: tag instances (Door, Pickup, Turret) with CollectionService and have one server Script/module per system (e.g. ServerScriptService/Systems/DoorSystem). Each system: for _, inst in GetTagged(tag) do setup(inst) end, plus GetInstanceAddedSignal(tag) for spawned/cloned/streamed-in instances and GetInstanceRemovedSignal(tag) to disconnect/cleanup (stream-out or destroy fires removal). Keep per-instance state in a table keyed by instance, use attributes for per-instance config (speed, damage), and shared logic like one Heartbeat loop for all 60 turrets instead of 60 loops. Client visuals use the same pattern locally.
B16: Give the driver's client network ownership of the car (vehicle seat assigns it, or SetNetworkOwner(driver) on the server) so steering/physics is responsive with no input latency; set back to server/nil when the driver leaves. Risk: the owning client simulates the car's physics, so an exploiter can teleport it, fly, speedhack, or fling other parts/players it collides with; ownership also lets them move connected assemblies. The server must still validate: speed/acceleration and position deltas against vehicle caps (sanity checks on Heartbeat), checkpoint order and lap times (no skipping), finish line crossing plausibility, that the driver is actually seated, and anything awarding rewards/currency; reset or kick on violations. Server Authority mode is the alternative if strict anti-cheat matters.
B17: Use an UnreliableRemoteEvent for the continuous aim/position stream (and lower the rate to ~10-20 Hz or send only on change). Constraints: payload over ~1,000 bytes is dropped; messages may be dropped (excess over throttle is discarded, not queued) and arrive out of order; no handler connected = discarded. Handling: keep the payload tiny (e.g. Vector3 / compressed angles + a sequence number); each message is a full state snapshot so a lost one doesn't matter; on the server ignore messages with sequence older than the newest seen; validate types, NaN/inf, magnitude and rate; interpolate on receivers. Keep important one-off events (fire, hit, reload) on a reliable RemoteEvent.
B18: Split NPCs across many Actors (e.g. 8-16 Actors with ~15-25 NPCs each; scripts in one Actor run serially, so one Actor gives no speedup). In each Actor's script use RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel (or task.desynchronize()) to do raycasts, spatial queries and path scoring in parallel (reads and Raycast are parallel-safe), store results locally, then task.synchronize() and apply writes (set positions, MoveTo, damage, instance changes) in the serial phase. Limitations: most property writes and creating/parenting/destroying instances are not allowed in parallel; require can't run in parallel and each Actor gets its own module copies; data between Actors goes via messages (SendMessage/BindToMessageParallel, copied, no functions) or SharedTable (atomic update/increment, update fn must be pure); budget work across frames and profile first (MicroProfiler).
B19: Turn on Workspace.StreamingEnabled. Defaults: StreamingMinRadius 64, StreamingTargetRadius 1024, StreamOutBehavior LowMemory (Opportunistic recommended for mobile memory); tune e.g. Min 128-256 / Target ~512-1024 based on testing. Set Model.ModelStreamingMode per model: Atomic for models that must arrive whole, Persistent only for small essentials (always replicated), Default/Nonatomic otherwise; enable improved ModelStreamingBehavior. Use Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync before teleporting players. Fix scripts: client code must not assume instances exist - use WaitForChild with timeouts and nil checks, use CollectionService added/removed signals to wire objects as they stream in/out (streamed-out parts are parented to nil), keep critical logic on the server, and QA with forced stream-out / small radii.
B20: 80 players x every 5 s = 960 SetAsync/min, plus other writes. Limits are now experience-wide (Write = 300 + 20 x CCU/min, shared with all servers and Open Cloud; per-server write budget 60 + 40 x players), and each request queue holds only 30; when full new requests fail (301-306/302 queue full) and saves are dropped. Also writing the same key too often and SetAsync overwriting blindly. Better: autosave every 60-180 s, staggered per player, saving only dirty data; save immediately on important events (purchases) with debounce; use UpdateAsync (with session lock) instead of SetAsync; check GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before writing; retry with exponential backoff; save on PlayerRemoving and BindToClose.
B21: Enable it in Studio: open the Assistant panel, the '...' menu -> Manage MCP Servers -> toggle 'Enable Studio as MCP server' (green indicator shows connected clients), then add it to your client (Quick connect, JSON config or CLI command) and restart the client. Tools include: list_roblox_studios, get_studio_state, search_game_tree, inspect_instance, script_read, script_search, script_grep, multi_edit, execute_luau, start_stop_play, get_console_output, screen_capture, character_navigation, user_keyboard_input, user_mouse_input, search_asset, insert_asset, upload_image, generate_mesh, generate_material, wait_job_finished, http_get. Call list_roblox_studios first (studio id changes per Studio restart); edits fail during Play.
B22: Three instance types: InputContext (a group of actions; Enabled, Priority, Sink), InputAction (one action, Type = Bool / Direction1D/2D/3D / ViewportPosition), InputBinding (child of an action mapping a KeyCode - keyboard, gamepad button - or a UIButton for touch, with modifiers/directional keys). An action signals via events: Pressed and Released (Bool), StateChanged(newState), and can be polled with GetState() (Fire() simulates). Precedence: give the menu's InputContext a higher Priority than the gameplay/default player scripts' contexts and set Sink = true so the inputs it binds are consumed and not passed to lower-priority contexts; enable it while the menu is open and disable (Enabled = false) on close. Default player scripts use IAS when Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem is enabled.
B23: UI Styling: a CSS-like system. StyleSheet holds StyleRule children; each StyleRule has a Selector (class name like TextButton, .Tag via CollectionService tags, #Name, pseudo-classes like :Hover, modifiers, @queries) and property values set via SetProperties({...}) (later/more specific rules win). Styles reach UI through a StyleLink placed in a ScreenGui/UI tree whose StyleSheet property points to the sheet; StyleDerive lets one sheet inherit another (e.g. a token sheet). Tokens: define attributes on a (token) StyleSheet, e.g. tokens:SetAttribute("Primary", Color3.fromRGB(...)), and reference them in rules as "$Primary"; swapping the token sheet (same names) switches themes.
B24: Age checks use facial age estimation (via a selfie video in the app, by a vendor), with ID verification or parental controls able to correct it; required for chat worldwide since January 2026. Users are placed in age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, 21+. By default a user can chat only with their own group and the adjacent groups (directly above/below), preventing e.g. under-16s chatting with adults; under-9s need parental consent and chat is off by default for younger kids. Trusted Connections let age-checked 13+ users chat more widely with people they know. Developers get no API returning age; use TextChatService (CanUsersChatAsync) and don't make gameplay depend on chat.
